title: Constructibility and uniform Tor bounds for point perfect extensions
statement: Fix finite-field datum D, a prime ell different from its characteristic, and a finite extension E of Q_ell [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let R be the lifted valuation ring, assumed Noetherian, and B the actual inverse limit of positive finite constant quotients [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For the actual coefficient map and point extension data [def-pod-point-derived-hom-models], let L be the recorded extension on objects and maps, exact and left adjoint to sections. If P is bounded with finite projective terms, then B[0] and L(P) are constructible integral derived-complete complexes [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and each has a single finite Tor-amplitude interval valid for every positive reduction [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text:
choose the DVR maximal ideal generated by the uniformizer. Identify the
inverse limit B of constant positive quotients with the constant-completion
sheaf through the canonical coefficient comparison, preserving its unit and
projections. The adic perfect-model completeness theorem applies to P and R[0].
Restriction through this coefficient comparison and the quotient/Koszul
completion equivalence identify its completeness with the actual augmented
reduction-tower completeness predicate. At each positive level, K-flatness
computes derived coefficient change by ordinary termwise extension. The finite
power comparisons, restricted along the projective splittings, identify this
with the constant reduced algebraic complex. Its terms and cohomology are
finite sets, since the coefficient quotient is finite; the corresponding
constant cohomology sheaves are constructible on the point stratum. Constant
realization is exact and preserves the original support. The reduced terms are
finite-free retracts, hence flat, so tensoring with every degree-zero module
sheaf preserves those same bounds. This gives one Tor interval for all levels.
If the recorded bounds are reversed, P is zero; use [0,0]. For R[0] the interval
is [0,0]. These completeness, constructibility and uniform Tor clauses are
precisely the two predicates asserted below.

theorem point_perfect_extension_constructible
    (hl : l ≠ D.p) [IsNoetherianRing (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))]
    (hmap : ∀ {M N : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l
      E))} (f : M ⟶ N),
      L.map f = eqToHom (hobj M) ≫ PointDerivedHom.extensionMorphism.{u, u}
        D.k (PointDerivedHom.coefficientSheaf.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true)
      (PointDerivedHom.coefficientMap.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true) f ≫ eqToHom (hobj N).symm)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L] [PreservesFiniteColimits L]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers
      l E))) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i, Module.Projective (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
      (P.X i) ∧ Module.Finite (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) (P.X
      i)) :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (PointDerivedHom.Modules.{u, u} D.k
      (PointDerivedHom.coefficientSheaf.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true)) := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E (Spec (.of D.k))
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (PointDerivedHom.Modules.{u, u} D.k
      (PointDerivedHom.coefficientSheaf.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true)) 0).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit (PointDerivedHom.ring.{u, u} D.k
      (PointDerivedHom.coefficientSheaf.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true))))) ∧
    finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E (Spec (.of D.k))
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((PointDerivedHom.extensionComplex.{u, u}
        D.k (PointDerivedHom.coefficientSheaf.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true)
      (PointDerivedHom.coefficientMap.{u, u} D.k l E 1 true) L adj).obj P))
